channel.title: all4dp
channel.description: Independent news and guides on 4D printing and smart materials

item.title: IIT Bhilai hydrogel changes shape on heating and pulls pollutants out of water
item.description: One printable gel does two jobs: it works as a soft actuator and it removes dyes and lead from wastewater.

item.title: IISc team 4D prints a self-folding breast duct model to study drug resistance
item.description: A flat printed sheet rolls into a duct-like tube in liquid, giving cancer cells a more realistic place to grow.

item.title: Concordia shapes carbon fibre wind turbine blades without moulds
item.description: Flat laminates curve into blade shapes as they cool, giving blades about 80% lighter than aluminium ones.

item.title: Korean team turns waste sulfur into a recyclable 4D printing material
item.description: Sulfur-rich plastics made from refinery by-product respond to heat, light and magnets, and can be melted and printed again.

item.title: Penn State prints a hydrogel “smart skin” that hides images and changes shape
item.description: A halftone printing pattern lets one hydrogel sheet control its look, its texture and its 3D form together.

item.title: 4D-printed stents from Waseda open at body temperature, no heater needed
item.description: A plasticiser tunes the shape memory polymer so the stent recovers at about 37 °C.
